deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It is a prose draft in which Riemann describes his current research program, apparently written for an official or autobiographical purpose. It is very probably a draft of the text Dedekind and Weber printed among the 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts / Naturphilosophie' in the Gesammelte Werke, which opens 'Die Arbeiten, welche mich jetzt vorzüglich beschäftigen, sind …'. Its content, item by item:

(1) The aim is to introduce the imaginary (complex variable) into the theory of transcendental functions beyond those already treated this way. Riemann names algebraic, exponential/circular, elliptic and Abelian functions as cases where this has been done 'with such great success'. He says the necessary general groundwork is in his Inaugural Dissertation (1851, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'), and gives an explicit cross-reference to Art. 20. In Art. 20 he outlines how the general method applies to functions defined by their boundary/branching behaviour, i.e. to other transcendental functions. Modern restatement: define analytic functions on Riemann surfaces by their singularities and boundary or periodicity behaviour (Dirichlet principle), and treat new transcendental classes this way. This programme was realised in his hypergeometric paper (1857) and the zeta paper (1859).

(2) Connected with this are new methods for integrating partial differential equations, already applied with success to several physical subjects. An insertion, partly struck through, specifies especially problems of electricity theory. The likely referents are potential theory and conformal-mapping methods for Laplace's equation Δu = 0, the method of characteristics / Riemann's method for hyperbolic equations, and his work on Nobili rings and electrostatics.

(3) His 'main work' is a new conception of the known laws of nature: their expression by means of different fundamental concepts. This is meant to make the experimental data on the interaction between heat [light, magnetism, electricity] usable. The page breaks off at 'Wärme'. The printed version continues to the effect of '… Licht, Magnetismus und Electricität zur Erforschung ihres Zusammenhangs möglich wurde', and then cites Newton, Euler and Herbart as influences.

No computations are made; nothing is filled in beyond identifying references.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page contains no computations.
The text is incomplete: it breaks off mid-sentence at 'zwischen Wärme'. The continuation is presumably on a lost or separate sheet, or is known only through the printed Werke version.

results.what: Programme of extending complex-function (Riemann-surface / Dirichlet-principle) methods from algebraic, elliptic and Abelian functions to other transcendental functions, with reference to Dissertation Art. 20
results.modern_name: Geometric/complex-analytic theory of special functions (e.g. Riemann's treatment of hypergeometric functions via monodromy; zeta function)

results.what: New methods of integrating PDEs, applied to physical (electrical) problems
results.modern_name: Potential theory / conformal mapping methods; Riemann's method for hyperbolic PDEs

results.what: Programme of a unified reformulation of natural laws (heat, light, magnetism, electricity) via new basic concepts

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known self-description of Riemann's research programme, already printed (in essentially this wording) in the Gesammelte Werke under the philosophical fragments. It contains no mathematics beyond statements of intent. Small wording variants in this draft are of minor philological interest only. An example is the struck-through insertion naming problems of electricity theory, which may be absent from the printed version (unsure).
transcription_corrections: The line beginning '2 (Vgl. diese Dissertation Art. 20.)' probably begins with an insertion or footnote mark, not the numeral 2. It is a parenthetical reference attached to item 1, not a second item.
In item 1 the struck-through words before 'den elliptischen' read 'mit so grossem' (possibly an anticipated 'mit so grossem Erfolge'), which Riemann then rewrote after 'Abelschen Functionen'.

Item 2 should read 'auf mehrere physikalische Gegenstände' ('Gegenstände' inserted above the struck-through 'Aufgaben'), followed by the deleted 'mit Erfolg angewandt habe'. The text continues 'namentlich auf Probleme aus der [Elec- struck] Electricitätslehre mit Erfolg angewandt habe'. The insertion 'namentlich … Electricitätslehre' appears partly struck through as well.
The final word 'Wärme' is fairly secure (compare the printed text: 'Wechselwirkung zwischen Wärme, Licht, Magnetismus und Electricität'). The page ends there.
